strings.SAF_THENEWORDER_DESC:
A monarchy without a monarch and a nation without direction, the Union of South Africa has found itself increasingly struggling to hold back the forces of unrest waiting to tear the nation asunder.

While the Boers have never managed to take power in the nation, their presence is felt as more and more they clamor for either representation or outright independence. Elsewhere, the Africans shout from the streets against a nation of segregation, if not in law than in practice. If its domestic issues were not enough, South Africa finds itself torn between two spheres, constantly being pressured by the Americans to join the OFN and the Germans to bow to the Reich.
strings.SAF_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
Lakes are few in Africa, islands even fewer, but there may as well be a sea between the Reichskommissariats of Hüttig and Schenck and the bright light burning at the tip of Africa. Backed against a wall, The Dominion of South Africa carefully slinks back and forth across the narrow tightrope of international diplomacy, speaking words of freedom and liberty to Washington and whispering promises of supremacy and segregation to the Reich.

So it has been since the end of the Second World War. Those that say the fighting ended in South Africa in 1945 are deluded or speaking in legalistic terms, for the battle for South Africa rages both abroad and at home. It helps nothing that the nation is a paradox in and of itself.
strings.SAF_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
South Africa is a dominion with no monarch wherein the minority governs the majority. Prime Minister De Villiers Graaff carefully plays his opponents against each other in order to maintain the shaky stability his party, the United Party, has established. But that stability comes at a price. To keep the Germans north of the Limpopo, South Africa cannot fully achieve the picture of liberty painted for the Americans. The throne of South Africa lays dusty and barren, a dominion only in name, but far from a republic.

Across the aisle, the powerful orations of Albert Hertzog echo out into the nation, attracting the Boer population to the National Party, a party established on cooperation with the Reich and the domination of white South Africans over the black. But they are not unopposed; all the while, the African National Congress vigorously fights to have their voice heard, figuratively and literally, as they have not been since the advent of South Africa.
strings.SAF_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
In the cities, the oppressed march in solidarity, demanding a continent free of division, meanwhile in the far flung outposts keeping watch on the Reichskommissariats, reports trickle in of villages burned and families slaughtered in the conflict between partisan forces and the German African Army. The Dominion truly does walk the tightrope, cautiously appeasing on all fronts.

The nation has many choices ahead of it; it can use the gifts exposed by De Beers with diamond mining to its advantage. It must balance foreign influence and profit as you attempt to maintain trade with the Pakt; and it must make sure to sway the upcoming election in its favor, for whatever choice is made there will shake South Africa one way or another. The conflict at the Cape is quickly becoming an inevitability; Prime Minister De Villiers Graaff must keep the country on the straight and narrow, for if South Africa were to slip from the high-wire, God only knows where she'd land.

strings.SAF_USA.1.desc:
The Nixon White House was defined by chaos. As phone line operators were overwhelmed by the sheer number of calls going to and from the White House, aides and staffers scrambled to form a cohesive image of what was happening across the Atlantic. Was Durban already about to fall to the Afrika-Schild, or was the press just fear-mongering? Was Hüttig receiving assistance from the SS, or was this just another rumor?

As the Executive Branch quickly shuffled into the Cabinet Room, Nixon watched them from the corner of his eye as he leaned forward in his chair, his right hand gripping a telephone as he listened to the other end. Kennedy unbuttoned his suit as he collapsed into a seat across from Nixon, with McNamara seating himself to the President's right. As the room waited in silence, Nixon finally concluded the phone call.

“Mhm. Tell Klein to deal with the press. And remind him that I'm cutting his staff in half.” Slamming the telephone down, Nixon straightened his posture before resting his arms on the mahogany conference table, papers scattered across it. Drawing a deep breath, Nixon began the meeting. “At this point, we can't, uh, not intervene. The situation isn't perfect, and we ought to find a way to send in the military before the—the Nazis, uh, crush the South Africans.” Nixon scoured the room for affirmation, seeing his cabinet respond only with tepid whispers of agreement.

Awkwardly adjusting himself in his seat, Nixon cleared his throat before continuing. “Get, uh, get every OFN diplomat on the line. I want them in New York within six hours.” Quietly, the cabinet exchanged glances before dismissing themselves. Nixon, however, had already decided what'd happen before the meeting began, and he was relieved when it ended.
strings.SAF_USA.1.a: Formality in a time of uncertainty.
strings.SAF_USA.2.desc:
The atmosphere was nothing but on edge. Despite the chill of New York City, wind maneuvering between the skyscrapers as dirty snow lined the streets below, the OFN headquarters' interior was intense with heat. The lights above slowly burned the OFN delegations as they whispered among themselves, tensely waiting for orders on how to vote on Security Resolution 13. Then, Richard Nixon emerged, and all eyes locked on him. Taking his seat at the table, he prepared the papers in his hand, swallowing before speaking into the microphone.

“Let me point out that this meeting helps unite our alliance and serves as a visible demonstration that the Organization of Free Nations remains behind her commitment to a free world,” Nixon began. “We are the remaining free nations of the world. Our defeat and humiliation in World War II promoted recklessness in the councils of those powers who have not yet abandoned their goals of world conquest. And so, the defense of freedom is everybody's business—not just America's business.”

“We cannot stand aloof and leave the fate of South Africa to the Boer rebellion and Afrika-Schild. We must stand ready in the face of Nazi aggression. To pass Security Resolution 13 means that we finally have in sight the stand for freedom we have been seeking these past decades. Thank you.” The delegations and spectators exchanged glances as the words set in and the room's anxiety subsided. An ear-blistering standing ovation followed.

Nixon, too, felt his anxiety subside. The vote was unanimous—hell, even Brazil ratified the resolution. There wasn't a goddamn chance that the Nazis put down their arms and withdrew within 24 hours—perfect. Not even Herblock and every bastard at the Post or the Times could somehow spin it into a failure. If the Free World could make its stand, '64 would be a breeze.
strings.SAF_USA.2.a: They'd rather die on their feet than live on their knees.
strings.SAF_USA.3.desc:
Sergeant Freeman sat upright on the olive green cot beneath him, a newspaper in his hands as the tent above protected him from the sun's scorching heat. It had been a rough two weeks. Every order he received was incoherent, and all the intelligence relayed to him turned out to be bogus. Hell- he'd led his men into the savannah and nearly engaged a South African platoon until they identified themselves. The sergeant's daydreaming ended when the headline caught his attention.

“OFN passes Security Resolution 14,” he read aloud to the rest of the tent. “Some good fucking news for once. Maybe they'll let us burn these krauts alive next.” The tent exchanged glances, some taking the news as a sign from God, others simply not caring. Private Wood, stretched out on his cot, stiffly turned his head toward the sergeant and opened his mouth.

“What's 'Security Resolution 14'?” Freeman skimmed through the newspaper before looking up, his hawkish gaze locking onto the private's.

“Sets up a single command structure instead of letting every one of our fucking allies run this shitshow their own way,” the sergeant barked. Reading through the newspaper once again, he adjusted himself before continuing. “Says here that Westmoreland's supposed to be leading it. They gave him some fancy title, 'Supreme Allied Commander'.” He let out a chuckle before finally topping it off. “And, it makes everyone use the OFN flag when fighting the krauts.”

Wood's eyes drifted to the tent's ceiling as he released a long, exaggerated sigh. “As long as it wins us this war faster,” he began with his distinct magnolia accent. “Can't take half measures no more. I mean, look what happened last time.” The private yawned, shifting in his cot before eventually dozing off. Whatever it takes, Freeman thought.
strings.SAF_USA.4.desc:
George Ball lifted the sleeve of his suit and checked his watch. Marching through the OFN's headquarters was nothing new to him, but the circumstances transformed it into an intimidating structure. Representing the United States was one thing, but he also had to contend with leading the Free World into South Africa. It was as if the moon, the stars, and all the planets had fallen on him. The weight had nearly broken him, but now was not the time to give up nor voice his reservations about South Africa.

Ball, now with the Security Council, leaned forward in the chair, his hands clasped together as they rested on the round table. The words “UNITED STATES” were displayed proudly on the nameplate that hung off the end as conversations echoed throughout the chamber. He tapped his foot on the floor, and when the session finally began and cameras trained onto him, he drew a deep breath.

“In many major capitals, there are already signs of deep concern at the present state of the refugee crisis,” Ball said into the microphone sternly. “Our joint and sole aim is to secure and maintain the political independence and territorial integrity of South Africa. But,” Ball began as he gripped a Washington Post article, lifting it in the air for all to see, “we must also be willing to assist the people that have experienced the horrors of Nazism directly.”

Pointing to the photograph on the front page of an African family marching through the exhausting savannah to escape the bloodshed, Ball continued. “Tens of thousands of refugees have already crossed the border, and that number will grow. We must consider a major effort by all of us to deliver economic and humanitarian aid to South Africa.” Ball's words were met with approval as the delegations nodded to each other, and when the voting began, they all cast 'aye' without hesitation.
strings.SAF_USA.5.desc:
Nothing Nixon did in the White House allowed him to escape the never-ending picketing of protestors outside. Even when he blasted classical music in the Oval Office at the loudest volume possible, it still could not drown out the yelling and marching of demonstrators. At night, muffled chanting kept him awake, his eyes straining as he stared at the Lincoln Bedroom's ceiling. He'd had enough.

Nixon sat alone in the darkness of the Oval Office. He stared at the briefing in front of him, his fists clenched as they rested on the Resolute Desk. He concentrated all his attention on the words printed on the paper. The noises had nearly faded into the background before Haldeman stepped into the room, and everything Nixon tried to forget rushed back to the front of his mind. Haldeman stared at Nixon for a moment, choosing his words carefully.

“They're protesting the war, sir.” Even as Haldeman spoke in his most soothing voice, it could not stop Nixon from taking it personally. Processing the words as fury emerged behind his eyes, Nixon stood up in disbelief before sending a stack of papers flying across the room.

“Bullshit!” Nixon exploded as any restraint he might've had vanished. “They're protesting a goddamn war against Nazis?” Haldeman opened his mouth to answer despite knowing the question was rhetorical. He couldn't get a word out before Nixon continued to seethe. “What the hell is the matter with those bastards! I mean, are they out of their goddamn minds?” Haldeman interjected, quickly correcting himself.

“No, sir—they're demonstrating in favor of the war. They want you to escalate it.” Nixon subdued himself, standing like a deer in headlights. Collapsing into his chair, he rested his chin in his hand as curiosity washed over him. Maybe they were right.
strings.SAF_USA.5.a: “Tell Safire I want to give a speech.”
strings.SAF_USA.6.desc:
Restaurant patrons listened to the radio's static, their food growing cold. Children's eyes were glued to the television screen as parents watched apprehensively from the kitchen. It was as if the nation came to a standstill. In the Oval Office, Nixon quietly shuffled the papers in his hands as the filming crew in front of him began counting down. The President drew a deep breath as he looked into the camera lens, and for a moment, he saw America looking back at him.

“Good evening, my fellow Americans. Tonight I want to talk to you on a subject of deep concern to all Americans and to many people in all parts of the world—the war in South Africa.” He forced the words out of his mouth, having paced the White House at night, restless as he tormented himself over the speech's content. “The war is necessary to continue. It is not the easy choice, but it is the right choice. Allowing South Africans' future to be determined by the victor of a military contest between themselves and the Boer rebellion, alongside the Afrika-Schild, would be a betrayal of our allies.”

He paused, assuming a gentle tone before continuing. “I considered the question of what choices we have if we are to end the war, and so, I have chosen to proclaim a national emergency concerning South Africa. This policy will help the war effort by allowing further mobilization of our military personnel and allowing the administration to direct the production of war materials.”

“With the confidence of our allies and confidence in ourselves, we will defend South Africa's freedom from Nazi aggression. If we succeed, generations to come will say of us now living that we mastered our moment, that we helped make the world safe for mankind. Thank you, and good night.” America processed the words, some excited, others anxious, as a fire ignited itself within. From that moment on, there was no backing down.
strings.SAF_USA.6.a: A sleeping giant awoken, filled with terrible resolve.
strings.SAF_USA.7.desc:
The crackle of gunfire and thunder of artillery seemed to cooperate to form a tapestry of smoke hiding brimstone in the distance, a beautiful vista captured by the video camera of reporter Barbara Walters' lone cameraman as their Sikorsky touched down on the South African helipad. As jets raced overhead, Walters and her singular crewman ran, hunched, into the Army Hospital.

“It is a chaotic scene here in South Africa, and we're here in a frontline hospital-” Walters' introduction was interrupted by a screaming, curly-haired superior to the men, yelling for his medics to begin triaging resources. Only later would Walters get the opportunity to interview the Technical Sergeant -as was declared by his uniform- at a sprawling vantage point of the valley, smoke still spiraling from the twisted wrecks of tanks and aircraft.

“So, tell us, sir, what is a day in your work like?” The Technical Sergeant looked down and smirked, then looked thoughtfully out to the mountains.

“Well, it's all work, honestly, there's rarely a moment of peace anyone can find out here, especially for the medics. It's hard on us all, but we can only focus on the happy little things, every chance we get.” The medic gestured to the vista. “This... is my escape from it all. I have always loved views like these, even when I was stationed in Alaska... as a matter of fact, I've something to show you all.” As the medic rooted around in a wide, rectangular bag tucked alongside a boulder, Walters recomposed herself.

“I see... why do you like these mountains so much, exactly, mister...?” Pulling a wide canvas out of his bag, the soldier's face seemed painted with pride.

“Please, call me Bob, and... well, look around. Beauty is everywhere- you only have to look to see it.”
strings.SAF_news.1.desc:
In New York City, the Organization of Free Nations passed Security Resolution 13 at the most contentious Security Council meeting of the alliance's history. Issuing a blistering condemnation of the Afrika-Schild's and Boer rebellion's breach of peace on the continent, the resolution also demands the withdrawal of all Schild forces from South Africa within 24 hours.

Ratified unanimously by all member states, including some observer states such as Brazil, many international observers doubt that the Schild will heed the deadline, instead continuing to press on. With many across the Free World shocked and angered by the assault on the last liberal state in Africa, it is anticipated that the OFN will inevitably rise to fight alongside South Africa.
strings.SAF_news.1.b: Let them cry all they want, it will make no difference.
strings.SAF_news.1.c: We'll defend South Africa as we would our own country!
strings.SAF_news.1.e: Are they willing to pay the price for victory?

strings.SAF_news.2.desc:
Two months ago, the war in South Africa began. Though the Organization of Free Nations' intervention took the initial steam out of the Schild's offensive, the war has bogged down into a slower, more brutal affair. Amidst military mobilization among the OFN's member states, vicious fighting consumes the savanna and the cities caught in the crossfire. However, many believe this will change soon.

As a wave of pro-war demonstrations washes over the United States, President Nixon issued a proclamation declaring the war a national emergency. Claiming the war is a threat to world peace in the form of Nazi expansionism, the national emergency authorizes the President to further mobilize the armed forces, likely for deployment to South Africa, and to revive past war production policies.
strings.SAF_news.2.a: Fathers continue to bury their sons.
strings.SAF_news.2.b: If it's total war they want, it's total war they'll have!

The discovery of diamonds at Kimberly, some one hundred years ago, has turned our country from a nation of farmers into a nation of miners - and since then, settlers all over the world came to the Cape in search of dreams of endless wealth, but the mining trade is no place for adventurers. The De Beers corporation, founded by Cecil Rhodes, and now run by Harry Oppenheimer from Cape Town has full control of the extraction and trade of the precious stones. By working closely with De Beers, not only have we opened doors to both the OFN and the Einheitspakt's economies, but we now have the means to turn our country into a proudly developed nation - if we can avoid the ire of the powers breathing down our necks, that is.

strings.SAF_Boer_Viet_Cong_desc: Armed Afrikaner paramilitary groups aren't a new phenomenon in South African history. However, many of these groups, bolstered by strong public support and RK influence, are conducting operations in South African territory with the goal of overthrowing the government. We must deal with this problem, or a free South Africa will cease to exist.
strings.SAF_The_Empty_Throne_desc: Whilst South Africa officially still has a monarchy, in reality the throne has remained empty since the death of King George VI. With the government never having recognised either Edward VIII or Elizabeth II out of a desire to antagonize neither the OFN nor the Einheitspakt, the position of the monarch has remained in limbo for nearly a decade. Whilst the government has so far remained unwilling to budge on the issue, public opinion is increasingly asking why South Africa continues to have a monarchy at all.
strings.SAF_Desperate_Neutrality_desc: Despite multiple attempts from the OFN to bring South Africa into their alliance, consecutive governments have consistently maintained a strong isolationist stance and claimed strict neutrality in the Cold War. Unwilling to antagonize the German Reich to the north, it would take a truly disastrous situation for our government to abandon this policy of neutrality.
strings.SAF_Divided_Nation_desc: Our nation is plagued by internal strife, crippled by political crisis. As the African National Congress calls for equal rights and self-determination, the government has so far refused all demands for reform. Now as terrorism spreads through the country, and the increasingly militant Boers denounce both the ANC and our government, the future of the nation seemingly rests on a knife-edge.
strings.SAF_Divided_Nation_2_desc: Our nation is plagued by internal strife, crippled by political crisis. As the African National Congress calls for equal rights and self-determination, the government has so far refused all demands for reform. Now as terrorism spreads through the country, and the increasingly militant Boers denounce both the ANC and our government, the future of the nation seemingly rests on a knife-edge.
strings.SAF_Uncle_Sam_Arrives_desc: Hope is not lost yet, America and the OFN came to our rescue! With the might of the Free World and the arsenal of democracy on our side, we will defeat the Boers and their damned German allies.
strings.SAF_SOG_advisors_desc: The Americans, who have been a greater aid to us already than we would like to admit, have sent their SOG group to us. The Spec Ops Study and Observation Group are here to help bolster our own troops against the superior forces of the Afrika-Schild. Their expertise in unconventional warfare will transform our forces into a creative army, which will be able to quickly react to the stratagems of our enemy. No longer will we waste precious lives in pointless defences. Instead, our men will blend into the landscape they know so well and strike out only when they know they can win. Let the Germans come for now, we will envelop their armies and drive them out soon enough.
strings.SAF_Cape_Town_Massacre_desc:
The Cape Town Massacre has forever stained our hands with blood! The already unrestful populace is extremely angered at such a violent act. They've been preparing, amassing, and calling for all to protest on the streets.

All around, people holding signs gather near local government buildings and some of the few policing forces we have refuse to stop this treacherous act.

Our road to recovery will be a herculean task.
strings.SAF_Army_Deployed_desc:
After the treacherous display from the police officers, it shows that we must take even further action to quell the Boers and their incitement of unrest. We must deploy our armed forces to areas of high resistance and continue the policing efforts employed.

While the populace will become more aggressive due to this seemgingly hostile action, it is necessary to ensure the stability of South Africa.
strings.SAF_ANC_Riots_desc: Protests and strikes called by the National Party have erupted across the nation have crippled our economy, something has to be done.
strings.SAF_icelandic_support_staff_desc:
The Icelandic Government has sent over a small envoy of highly trained doctors and nurses to help instruct and aid our young medics. Iceland possesses one of the most advanced healthcare systems, so their experienced systems and procedures used will be taught to us.

With this, we hope we can prevent more deaths whether on the battlefield or on the homefront.
strings.SAF_our_darkest_hour_desc: As the Germans and Boers begin to overwhelm the country, this is most certainly the darkest hour in the life of our young republic. The situation may look bleak, yet despite the challenge now face we shall fight on and we shall never surrender!
strings.SAF_boer_insurgency_desc: The Boers plan to fight a protracted war once more, striking us the further we push into their territory. Our efforts to uproot their hideouts and warding off their raids have borne little fruit.
strings.SAF_boer_insurgency2_desc: The Boers plan to fight a protracted war once more, striking us the further we push into their territory. Our efforts to uproot their hideouts and warding off their raids have borne little fruit.
strings.SAF_surprise_attack_desc:
When the Boers took up arms en masse against the South African state, we were caught with our pants down. They moved swiftly and unexpectedly in organizing themselves into a ramshackle state with an organized militia, fully capable of dealing crippling blows to our forces. We are still reeling from the shock.

Without a doubt, we must step back and re-organize our efforts before we proceed, else we risk being blindsided by the Boers once more.
strings.SAF_Coluna_Infernal_desc: Portugal produced perhaps one of the finest self-trained guerrilla fighters the world has ever seen. Their years of experience, ruthless methods and knowledge of the terrain have proven tremendously effective in both clearing the way and eliminating pockets of resistances, earning them nicknames such as 'Os Terriveis', 'A Coluna Infernal', the 'Terrible Ones'.
strings.SAF_Coluna_Infernal_2_desc: Portugal produced perhaps one of the finest self-trained guerrilla fighters the world has ever seen. Their years of experience, ruthless methods and knowledge of the terrain have proven tremendously effective in both clearing the way and eliminating pockets of resistances, earning them nicknames such as 'Os Terriveis', 'A Coluna Infernal', the 'Terrible Ones'.
strings.SAF_chaos_behind_lines_desc: Missing material caches, wrong coordinates, massive supply issues, random surprise attacks. These problems started to appear pretty recently, and as consequence the frontline has become much harder to control. If we cannot turn the situation quickly enough, this chaos will overwhelm our army.
strings.SAF_American_training_desc: With the war in full swing, America brought over material support and military advisors to support our army. We can use the expertise coming from the strongest military in the world so our troops can learn the modern art of war on the field of battle.
strings.SAF_Unconventional_Tactics_desc: As the war endures, we find ourselves under ever increasing pressure from the combined forces of the Reichskommissariats and the Boer insurgency. To counter these pressures, we have developed a plethora of robust and unconventional stratagems to employ against the Germans and Boers. Ambushes. Insurgency. Psychological warfare. Fighting behind their lines. Every step closer our enemies take towards our borders will make them grow ever more fearful of what tricks the South Africans have up their sleeves. More often than not, our foes find their ranks already noticeably depleted by the time they reach the lines of conventional battle.
strings.SAF_Unconventional_Tactics_2_desc: As the war endures, we find ourselves under ever increasing pressure from the combined forces of the Reichskommissariats and the Boer insurgency. To counter these pressures, we have developed a plethora of robust and unconventional stratagems to employ against the Germans and Boers. Ambushes. Insurgency. Psychological warfare. Fighting behind their lines. Every step closer our enemies take towards our borders will make them grow ever more fearful of what tricks the South Africans have up their sleeves. More often than not, our foes find their ranks already noticeably depleted by the time they reach the lines of conventional battle.
strings.SAF_Unconventional_Tactics_RK_desc: On the open battlefield, our forces had no trouble whatsoever with the outdated army of South Africa. We were able to quickly overrun them in similar fashion to the Second World War. However, recent developments have given us more trouble than we would like to admit. The South Africans are beginning to utilize methods of warfare that we had not anticipated. The enemy now hides, making full use of their landscape to avoid direct confrontation. We now face ambushes and traps rather than conventional battles. Our soldiers are struggling to adapt to this dramatic shift in the war. Unless we can adjust equally as quickly, we suspect that the fight will rage on for longer than we could have anticipated.
strings.SAF_Unconventional_Tactics_RK_2_desc: It seems that sudden ambushes and concealed explosives were the least of our concerns. Even as our troops begin to adjust to guerrilla warfare, the South Africans have begun changing their tactics one again. Ambushes are starting to take place behind the lines, focusing on our supply columns and bases. The men are suffering mentally from the constant raids too, as no matter where they are, the chance of an attack becomes increasingly common. The structure of South African divisions are shifting too. When captured, they have nothing of value to tell us, as their units now operate independently from their own high command. We must meet this problem head on.
strings.SAF_Unconventional_Tactics_RK_3_desc: The days of swift victory over South African soldiers seem like an almost distant memory now. Now we find only new and frustrating surprises on the front lines and behind them. Our troops might take several miles of ground in a day, only to be driven back by their camp being set ablaze during the night. The issues with supplies continue, as the South Africans always seem to know which routes we are using, as we discover when our trucks detonate mines buried in the dirt. Even our air force now useless, as trying to bomb underground targets is a gamble at best. What scant few casualties we inflict pales in comparison to what the South Africans inflict with each of their raids. Nowhere is safe now, and there is very little we can do about it.
strings.SAF_Caribbean_support_staff_desc: Scientists and engineers may be all the West Indies can offer to support us in our fight, but they have performed to a standard of excellence in their tasks assigned. Under their watch, roads which lay incomplete for months were finished in weeks, kinks both known and heretofore unknown in the Force's weaponry were summarily ironed out, and techniques were introduced which improved our research labs' productivity by leaps and bounds. We are quite indebted to the West Indies for the exemplary individuals they have sent in our aid.
strings.SAF_sao_tome_desc: São Tomé and Príncipe is a calm, underdeveloped backwater off the coast of Iberian Guinea. At least, until the Iberians came to an agreement with us to use it as a refueling and supply station. Since then, it has been a vital stop for transport ships and warships alike - in addition to its close proximity to Reichskommissariat Zentralafrika, allowing for reconnaissance and covert operations behind enemy lines to expand.
strings.SAF_lessons_first_civil_war: Lessons of the First Civil War
strings.SAF_lessons_first_civil_war_desc: Back during the South African War, attacks by Boer guerillas were a constant and traumatizing occurrence, cutting down units with little more than a half dozen men. Now though, with the Volkstaat's collapse, the tables have turned. The tactics of the Boers shall now be their, as well as the rest of our enemies', worst nightmares, just as it was ours.
strings.SAF_wraak_desc: We've been through a lot. Our nation first suffered siege and fell under the grip of the Germans. Then, under the Boers, our people were forced out, made to either die in camps further north or forced to labor in the cities we used to call home. While we've dragged through the mud and back, we're still kicking. There is an apt word to describe the feelings we harbor towards our enemies that can be taken from their own dictionary: “Wraak”, or in English, revenge.
strings.SAF_dissident_military_desc: The military of the reestablished Republic of South Africa is far from some of the organized and cohesive military units that surround it. Its ranks comprise members from both sides of the last civil war, and as a result disputes and fights amongst ranks are a common sight. This has hindered the military from acting in a cohesive manner, limiting combat effectiveness.

In the province of Natal, which contains [?719.SAF_voter_percent]% of voters, we estimate voters are {719_getsafmonarchysupport} the monarchy.
